newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rejects peace summit, Tutsis flee Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rejects peace summit, Tutsis flee Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire said on Monday it would not attend the first summit called to try and deal with fighting and a looming refugee tragedy in its eastern provinces.
Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda reiterated the government's charges of aggression against Rwanda which Zaire accuses of helping Tutsi rebels seize part of eastern Zaire.
"We are definitely not going to take part in talks in Nairobi, and could not talk while our territory is occupied by foreign forces," Kamanda told Reuters.
Anti-Tutsi sentiment mounted in the vast Central African country with hundreds of frightened ethnic Tutsis escaping into neighbouring Congo or going into hiding.
Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi expects to receive the leaders of Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Cameroon for talks in Nairobi on Tuesday.
Soldiers of Rwanda's Tutsi-led army have taken part in some of the fighting in Zaire's eastern border which sent hundreds of thousands of refugees, mostly Rwandan Hutus, fleeing for their lives.
Ethnic Tutsis were attacked or harassed during demonstrations in Kinshasa last week. Many Tutsi families have reported missing relatives.
"These problems in the east have for once got everybody together, the opposition, the army, the government. We don't want to deal with the Rwandans," said mechanic Jonas Mukendi.
Demonstrators last week called on part-Tutsi Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo to step down, saying he had not done enough to prosecute the war. They then attacked Tutsi homes and property.
About 400 Banyamulenge Tutsis in dugout canoes, escaped into Congo on Monday, joining some 200 others who have crossed into Brazzaville in the past two weeks.

The Congo river runs between Brazzaville and Kinshasa, forming a natural frontier between Zaire and Congo. The fleeing Tutsis would have had to sneak through unguarded crossing points or bribed their way through.
"If we try to get out by the official channels we get stopped at the border and accused of being the enemy," said one Tutsi in hiding in Kinshasa.
The Zaire army on Monday paraded before reporters people it said were Rwandan Tutsi prisoners captured in recent fighting.
The 10 prisoners, one of whom claimed to be of Zairean origin, were brought to army headquarters with documents identifying them as members of the Rwandan Patriotic Army (RPA).
Fighting flared two weeks ago following attempts by provincial authorities backed by the army to expel Banyamulenge Tutsis whose ancestors settled from Rwanda 200 years ago.
Zaire accuses them of being surrogates of Rwanda's Tutsi army which won civil war in 1994, sending more than one million majority Hutus fleeing into Zaire.
Rwanda and Zaire have been at loggerheads since the arrival in Zaire of the Hutus, whose hardliners massacred up to a million Rwandan Tutsis or moderate Hutus before fleeing.
